item.title: Playoffs: Wolfson completes high school volleyball season sweep
item.description: On the volleyball court , Averie Porter thrives on energy. On Tuesday night, she never slowed down. "This time, we kept [the energy] high the whole time, even when we were down, and it really helped us a lot," the Wolfson sophomore said. The Wolfpack punched their ticket for the weekend by defeating Bolles 25-19, 25-23, 25-10 in the Florida High School Athletic Association Region 1-3A volleyball quarterfinals on Oct. 20. Whenever Wolfson needed a key point, Porter usually wasn't far away, smashing kill after kill with intensity at the net to continue her excellent season. Bolles (14-11) built leads of 13-9 and 22-19 in the second set, but Monica Mina triggered a 5-0 run to swing the momentum back the Wolfpack's way. The Wolfpack (20-6) wrapped up the second and dominated the third to eliminate the Bulldogs for the second consecutive year. "We switched up the rotations a little bit in the last few games, and we found it [the right rhythm]," Wolfpack coach Brianna Kerley said. "It worked and it clicked." Wolfson next travels Oct. 24 to top seed Pensacola Catholic (24-4), which swept past Baldwin. Baldwin ends the year at 19-6. REGION 1-2A Trinity Christian (23-6) won a rematch of their district final, 25-15, 25-20, 25-20 over Episcopal. The Conquerors next play Oct. 24 against Tallahassee Maclay or Orlando First Academy. For Episcopal (16-13), Alexis Galani finished with 12 kills, Vi Janikowski supplied 27 assists and Lacey Reed had 24 digs. REGION 1-1A Top seed Christ's Church improved to 20-7 with a 25-20, 19-25, 25-15, 25-14 victory over Gainesville Countryside Christian (14-11). Covenant School (17-8) punched its own ticket to the next round with a 25-22, 19-25, 25-16, 25-21 victory at Tallahassee Community Christian (21-6). They will next play against Beaches Chapel (19-5), which cruised to a 25-12, 25-12, 26-24 sweep of Wakulla Christian (16-3). item.description: Ben Stiller shakes David Robinson's hand during Game 1 of the NBA Finals at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, on Wednesday, June 3, 2026. "It's just great to be in the mix and great to know we have a shot," Robinson said. "We have great young talent. I'm confident with Steph Castle. I'm confident with Dylan Harper. I'm confident with our young team. I think they're going to show up night in and night out." The Spurs reached the Finals last season after beating the defending champion Oklahoma City Thunder in seven games in the Western Conference finals. They fell to the New York Knicks in five games. Robinson said the postseason experience will help the young team grow. "Our guys were too young," he said. item.title: Walker Kessler Embracing Lofty Laker Expectations
item.description: Walker Kessler understands. He knows what the standard is as a Los Angeles Laker. He knows what the team gave up —then committed on the books —to pair him with Luka Dončić. “It’s just depending on how you look at it,” Walker said after Tuesday’s practice. “You can look at it from two perspectives and I think the more energy you give, you know, the positive perspective looking at this opportunity, the less time obviously you spend worrying about the pressure.” The 25-year-old will get his first opportunity to prove his energy on Wednesday night when the Lakers host the Warriors in their season opener. It will also mark his first NBA regular-season game since October 31, 2025, after undergoing season-ending shoulder surgery. “I think it’s gonna be a lot of fun, Kessler said. “I think it’s gonna be a lot of nerves going into the game. But as soon as the whistle blows, I think the rest of it will take care of itself.” Oct 16, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler (14) scores on a reverse layup in the first quarter against the Denver Nuggets at Crypto.com Arena. Mandatory Credit: Jon Endow-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) What will Walker Kessler’s role be for the Lakers? Pairing an athletic center alongside Dončić this offseason was a top priority for the Lakers. His 7’2″ frame allows him to be a true lob threat in the pick-and-roll, and his elite shot-blocking ability and paint presence solidify him as the Lakers’ defensive anchor. “[Dončić’s and Austin Reaves’] ability to see the floor without even really looking… it’s a savant thing,” Kessler said when asked about playing alongside the Lakers’ star backcourt. “They’re exceptional players, extremely gifted. item.title: Collin Sexton‘s injury status for Lakers’ season opener vs. Warriors, revealed
item.description: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Collin Sexton‘s injury status for Lakers’ season opener vs. Warriors, revealed appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . LOS ANGELES – The Los Angeles Lakers are set to open the 2026-27 regular season on Wednesday night against the Golden State Warriors, and one of the biggest questions surrounding the team in the final days of training camp was the injury status of Collin Sexton . Collin Sexton was sidelined for the entirety of preseason due to what was described as a lower leg injury, and he only recently begun participating fully during Lakers practice. With the first injury report of the season released, the nine-year veteran was officially listed as questionable against the Warriors due to a right soleus strain. Second-year wing Adou Thiero (left knee effusion) and rookie guard Cameron Carr (right oblique strain) were both ruled out. Following Lakers’ practice on Monday, Sexton spoke to reporters for the first time since Media Day, and acknowledged that while he was certainly feeling better in terms of the injury, playing in the season opener was not a forgone conclusion. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “We’re taking it day by day,” Sexton said after Lakers’ practice on Monday. “I had a really good practice … it felt good. Super excited to be back out there with the guys, so I look forward to it.” Sexton was signed by the Lakers in the offseason via free agency after splitting last year between the Charlotte Hornets and Chicago Bulls. He’s coming off a season in which he averaged a combined 15.4 points, 2.3 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.1 steals with splits of 48.5 percent shooting from the field, 40.1 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 85.5 percent shooting from the free-throw line. The expectation coming into the regular season was that he would anchor the second unit as the primary ball-handler. Without him available for preseason, the Lakers’ reserve ball-handling was shaky, leading to head coach JJ Redick to bring Quentin Grimes off the bench in the final preseason game to help alleviate the turnover issues. While observing from the sidelines, Sexton is well aware of how he can help the team , and he’s just looking forward to getting out on the court in official capacity. “Super eager, I’m super eager,” Sexton exclaimed. “But I have to just continue to take it day by day and continue to do the work in the weight room as well as the work on the training room table.” Related: Lakers’ Austin Reaves hilariously reveals reaction to LeBron James in 76ers uniform Related: JJ Redick eager to unlock Walker Kessler’s ‘All-Star level,’ but there’s a catch

item.title: Michigan State basketball misses revenge chance in sloppy loss vs UConn
item.description: EAST LANSING – There would be no revenge for Tom Izzo on Dan Hurley. Not for Michigan State basketball’s exhibition loss a year ago to Connecticut nor its season-ending defeat to the Huskies in the Sweet 16. Even if this one didn’t count. The sixth-ranked Spartans struggled with No. 5 UConn’s experience and size en route to a 78-70 exhibition loss on Tuesday, Oct. 20, at Breslin Center. Jeremy Fears Jr. finished with 23 points and eight assists and played through an ankle injury he suffered early in the second half. The fourth-year junior went 12-for-14 at the free-throw line and made 5 of 12 shots from the field. Freshman Jasiah Jervis scored 11 points with two 3-pointers off the bench, the only other MSU player to reach double figures. Nik Khamenia had 19 points and Silas Demary Jr. 16 for UConn, which lost in the national title game to Michigan in April after eliminating the Spartans. The Huskies led by as many as 15 points with 5:51 to play, but Izzo’s team could get no closer than seven in the final four minutes. Here are the starting five thoughts after MSU’s second of three exhibition games: No. 1: Fears factor In a flash, Fears gave a glimpse of his past and what Izzo and MSU fans hope is the future return of his explosiveness. And in another moment, the Spartans’ worst fear. With 6:22 left in the first half, Fears took the ball at the top of the key and zoomed past Demary and Hines downhill into the lane. As 6-6 Colben Landrew stepped up to challenge him, the smaller Fears – 6-2 in your program, 6-foot at the NBA Scouting Combine in May – didn’t stop. It was reminiscent of the driving and leaping ability Fears flashed briefly as a freshman in 2023, before he was shot in the upper left thigh that Christmas and missed the rest of that season while recovering from his bullet wounds. Early in the second half, though, Fears scared the raucous Breslin crowd into silence. The preseason national and Big Ten player of the year drove down the left side for a scooped-in layup but landed on the Landrew with 17:53 to play. Fears grabbed at his left ankle and lower leg while laying on the court, got back up and hobbled to the bench, checking himself out of the game and immediately going to the training staff. His stay was brief. Fears received treatment and checked back into the game with 15:44 to play, with Izzo telling him to take it easy. Jeremy Fears Jr. finished with 23 points and eight assists and played through an ankle injury he suffered early in the second half. The fourth-year junior went 12-for-14 at the free-throw line and made 5 of 12 shots from the field. Freshman Jasiah Jervis scored 11 points with two 3-pointers off the bench, the only other MSU player to reach double figures. Nik Khamenia had 19 points and Silas Demary Jr. 16 for UConn, which lost in the national title game to Michigan in April after eliminating the Spartans. The Huskies led by as many as 15 points with 5:51 to play, but Izzo’s team could get no closer than seven in the final four minutes. Here are the starting five thoughts after MSU’s second of three exhibition games: No. 1: Fears factor In a flash, Fears gave a glimpse of his past and what Izzo and MSU fans hope is the future return of his explosiveness. And in another moment, the Spartans’ worst fear. With 6:22 left in the first half, Fears took the ball at the top of the key and zoomed past Demary and Hines downhill into the lane. As 6-6 Colben Landrew stepped up to challenge him, the smaller Fears – 6-2 in your program, 6-foot at the NBA Scouting Combine in May – didn’t stop. JEREMY FEARS JR. ❕❕❕ Subscribe/watch on B1G+ https://t.co/x4CcGuKUVZ pic.twitter.com/cswGRKGEwX — Michigan State Men's Basketball (@MSU_Basketball) October 20, 2026 Fears elevated over Landrew and delivered a ferocious tomahawk dunk as Hines tried to swat at it from behind. It was reminiscent of the driving and leaping ability Fears flashed briefly as a freshman in 2023, before he was shot in the upper left thigh that Christmas and missed the rest of that season while recovering from his bullet wounds. Early in the second half, though, Fears scared the raucous Breslin crowd into silence. The preseason national and Big Ten player of the year drove down the left side for a scooped-in layup but landed on the Landrew with 17:53 to play. Fears grabbed at his left ankle and lower leg while laying on the court, got back up and hobbled to the bench, checking himself out of the game and immediately going to the training staff. His stay was brief. Fears received treatment and checked back into the game with 15:44 to play, with Izzo telling him to take it easy. THE INJURY: Jeremy Fears Jr. returns to UConn vs MSU exhibition after injury scare No. 2: Rotation review UConn wanted to match MSU’s toughness early, and it did with 6-8 Khamenia (a Duke transfer), 6-11 Oskar Giltay (a Stanford transfer) and 6-7 Jayden Ross. Izzo started 7-2 transfer Anton Bonke at center but quickly went with 6-11 Jesse McCulloch to replace him. At the outset of the second half, 7-2 freshman Ethan Taylor replaced Bonke in the starting group, along with Fears, Jordan Scott, Coen Carr and Cam Ward. Izzo mixed and matched lineups frequently, using 11 players in the first half. Jasiah Jervis was MSU’s first guard off the bench, while Carlos Medlock Jr. spelled Fears intermittently and when he went to the bench. The Spartans cut a 30-22 halftime deficit to two points with Medlock and Taylor in the game together as part of an 8-2 opening salvo. Carr struggled all game, going scoreless with just three rebounds in 15 first-half minutes. After halftime, the senior swingman had eight points and two more rebounds, finishing 2-for-7 from the field. Scott maybe showed the most growth from the last time MSU and UConn met in March, when the Huskies sent the Spartans out of the NCAA Tournament in the Sweet 16. The sophomore showed physical defense with his improved strength, getting his long arms to jar balls loose and scrapping with UConn for jump ball tie-ups. Scott finished with seven points on 3-of-8 shooting with five rebounds in 30 minutes. After scoring 20 points in MSU’s win over Incarnate Word to open exhibition play, Jesse McCulloch had just six points and four rebounds in 16 minutes against UConn. Ward got the start after sitting out the exhibition opener and finished with four points and six rebounds in 24 minutes. At least for this matchup, Kur Teng and Kaleb Glenn appeared to be the odd men out of the 11-man group. Teng got an extended run late with the Spartans trying to get back into it but missed all three of his 3-point attempts in his 10 minutes of action. Glenn went scoreless with one rebound in 10 minutes. Bonke also did not play in the second half after getting just 6 minutes in the first half, finishing with two points and three rebounds. No. 3: Plenty to work on Even though it was an exhibition, Izzo won't be happy with the sloppiness early on, along with one of the weaknesses of his team in recent years. MSU had 10 first-half turnovers, four of them by Fears, but they committed just two in the second half. At the free-throw line, the Spartans showed issues, making 5-of-8 in the opening half and finishing 25-of-34. But Izzo also will be miffed with how MSU struggled to guard the 3-point arc throughout the game. The Huskies went 10-for-25 and also missed a number of open looks from deep, including multiple late when the game was out of reach. Meantime, the Spartans equally had major outside shooting issues themselves. They made just 3 of 20 from 3-point range and struggled to get back in it late without that deep shooting. No. 4: Freshman focus The 6-4 Jervis had moments where he looked unfazed by the jump in competition, burying a 3-pointer on his first shot after entering the game at the 15:35 mark of the first half. But he also learned a valuable lesson when he tried to drive into the teeth of the Huskies’ back line and got stuffed for a turnover. Medlock also had moments where the bigger and more experienced Huskies guards neutralized him, and the 5-11, 178-pound point guard finished with two points on 1-for-7 shooting with one assist. Taylor showed some tenacity in spurts and an ability to score deep in the post. He had five points and two rebounds. The fourth freshman, forward Julius Avent, did not play. No. 5: Up next After opening with a win over Incarnate Word a month before the Nov. 2 regular-season opener against Quinnipiac, the Spartans head to Milwaukee on Sunday to wrap up exhibition play against Shaka Smart and Marquette (1 p.m./streaming on YouTube). item.title: 🙄Atlético Nacional stumble against Cúcuta Deportivo and raise doubts
item.description: 🙄Atlético Nacional stumble against Cúcuta Deportivo and raise doubts Atlético Nacional suffered a bitter 1-0 defeat away to Cúcuta Deportivo in the Liga BetPlay 2026-II. The hosts capitalized on an early goal and defended effectively, securing a vital result that moves them into the top eight qualifying spots and gives them much-needed breathing room in the relegation standings. Lack of goals and a creative block in attack The match followed the same frustrating script as the encounter with Llaneros in Villavicencio weeks earlier. Despite James Rodríguez's efforts and vision, the 'Verdolaga' lacked the cutting edge to break down Cúcuta's solid defense. The absence of key attacking players such as Alfredo Morelos, Cristian 'Chicho' Arango and, more recently, Ian Poveda took a heavy toll on their finishing inside the opposition's penalty area. Forced reliance on youth and a fading aura of invincibility The string of absences forced the coaching staff to turn to the academy, with the team finishing the match with several youngsters on the pitch and an average age of just 21.7. While Atlético Nacional remain near the top of the table and have games in hand to secure their place in the final-stage groups, the 'King of Cups' no longer look as unbeatable as they did last season, showing vulnerabilities when playing away from home. The Boston Celtics may not have started the season off the way they would have wanted to after crumbling in the fourth en route to suffering a 121-113 loss to the Detroit Pistons. However, they have to be very encouraged by what they saw from offseason trade acquisition Paul George . George, whom the Celtics received in the Jaylen Brown trade, put on a show in his official debut for the team. In just 31 minutes of play, the 36-year-old star popped off for 38 points on 12-21 shooting from the field (7-12 from beyond the arc) — being Boston’s biggest star of the night amid shooting struggles from Jayson Tatum. Nonetheless, George does not care at all if he had a good game in a loss. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I’m not a moral victory guy. It means nothing,” George said after the game, per ESPN. George did put up the most points for any player making their Celtics debut, and considering how many talented players have donned the franchise’s iconic green and white, this is no mean feat. The Celtics have to be feeling a bit vindicated as well for their decision to trade Brown, the man who averaged 29/7/5 last season as the first option amid Tatum’s injury, for George. Fans thought that it was bonkers for the Celtics to trade a superstar talent like Brown, who’s still in his prime, for someone like George, who is making the same money but has looked over the hill. George played in just 78 games combined over the past two seasons, so there are legitimate availability concerns surrounding him as well. But George, who is a huge competitor, knows that huge individual performances don’t mean much if it ends in defeat. He is currently in his 17th NBA season, and he has scored all the points and made all the threes he can. Playing winning basketball, however, is what matters to him the most, making his incredible Celtics debut all the more bittersweet. Likewise, an eagle is 50 books and a tournament won is 1,000. Since creating his Tony Finau Foundation Literacy Center in West Valley two years ago, Finau says literacy levels at his center have increased 19% while also assisting with vision screenings, food distribution and other essentials. “With the support I have here, and with this type of momentum, I don’t see why ... we can’t achieve” (the 100% goal for child reading proficiency), Finau said. “We’re so extremely proud to just be part of this initiative and pushing this (agenda) in Utah. item.title: 'We don't want you!': Knicks fans erupt with daunting LeBron James chant vs. 76ers
item.description: 'We don't want you!': Knicks fans erupt with daunting LeBron James chant vs. 76ers originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Knicks are finally getting their one shining moment after 53 years of waiting. Jalen Brunson and Co. hoisted their NBA championship banner at Madison Square Garden. But one raging team wants to spoil this special night. It is none other than the Philadelphia 76ers led by LeBron James, Jaylen Brown, and Joel Embiid. Knicks fans show obvious disdain whenever these rivals visit. They made that known when the veteran superstar was at the line. Knicks fans erupt to chant and distract 76ers' James at the free-throw line There is a long history of rivalry between the Knicks and the 76ers. These two franchises have duked it out in the Atlantic Division for decades. They met on NBA Opening Night. One squad, led by Jalen Brunson, is expected to cap a career's worth of work by hoisting the NBA championship banner at Madison Square Garden. The other? Well, their Larry O'Brien hopes have just started. They have already seen what Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, and V.J. Edgecombe are capable of. Now, they also have LeBron James and Jaylen Brown on the squad. Knicks fans are notorious for doing everything they can to make their Atlantic Division rivals falter on their home court. So, what did they do against the 76ers? The crowd made it clear that James wasn't welcome at MSG. They started chanting, "We don't want you!" at the top of their lungs to distract the veteran 76ers star, via Justin J. Lopez. Fans chant “WE DON’T WANT YOU!” At LeBron James. #Knicks #AlwaysKnicks #NewYorkForever https://t.co/bWfW7hdvQr — Justin J. Lopez (@stellar_jl319) October 20, 2026 The chant did get to James at the free-throw line. He missed the opportunity at the charity stripe when the Knicks crowd erupted. Notably, this is a mind trick Knicks fans are playing on James, and it goes both ways. First, he lives in New York City instead of Philadelphia despite playing for the 76ers. His daily commute by a Fanatics-sponsored helicopter has caused quite a stir. Second, recent reports have surfaced that James wanted to be drafted by the Knicks instead of the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2003. In both scenarios, Knicks fans have already decided to make him unwelcome at their home stadium. More than that, the Knicks crowd also seemed to get in James' head even when the ball is live. At the halfway mark of the third quarter, the 76ers star didn't look like his normal self. He managed only 11 points on 55.5% shooting and went 0-for-3 from three-point range despite three attempts from deep. James is making an effort to impact the game in a different way. He has dropped five assists to help with the 76ers' offensive rhythm. Defensively, Coach Nick Nurse has also seen him grab four rebounds while getting two steals. The 76ers and Knicks still have a quarter and a half to play in this NBA season opener. Howe

item.title: ‘We don’t want you’ – Knicks fans chant brutal message at LeBron James during his 76ers debut
item.description: Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images Philadelphia 76ers superstar LeBron James got a cold reception from the home fans of the New York Knicks upon his debut on opening night. The NBA schedule-makers decided to make opening night one of the biggest nights of the regular season by pitting two of the biggest moments against one another. The Knicks have waited for a championship for 53 years and raised their banner on October 20. They did it with divisional rivals, the Philadelphia 76ers, in the building, featuring LeBron James for his debut with the franchise in his 24th NBA season. Knicks fans let LeBron James know their true feelings about him During James’ first trip to the free-throw line in the first half, Madison Square Garden erupted into chants of ‘We don’t want you’ toward the 41-year-old. The chanting is a clear reference to James’ open admission that he would have joined the Knicks in the 2026 offseason if the franchise had not won a championship already. The appetite from the organisation to bring James into the fold after their title success was also extremely low. Players such as Jalen Brunson made it clear in interviews that the Knicks were not interested in pursuing LeBron in free agency the same way teams such as the Cavaliers, Heat, and Warriors did. While it’s been confirmed that LeBron did not want to join the Knicks after they won the championship, the franchise proved that they never needed LeBron in the first place to make their title dreams come true. The Knicks have been floated as a potential LeBron destination going all the way back to the 2003 NBA Draft, with the Knicks making multiple aggressive pursuits of James over the last two decades. With James also having an affinity for the historic franchise and their iconic arena, Madison Square Garden, it seemed the cards could have aligned in 2026 if the Knicks failed to win the title. However, they did secure the championship they have always craved, nixing any plans of an emergency LeBron addition. The 76ers trail the 58-54 Knicks at halftime, with LeBron putting up five points, four rebounds and five assists in 16 minutes of action. item.title: Denver Broncos Super Bowl Champion Gets Good News
item.description: Ex-Broncos kicker Brandon McManus has found a new NFL home. Getty The Denver Broncos just missed out on an on-field reunion with Super Bowl champion and veteran placekicker Brandon McManus. “The #Rams are signing veteran kicker Brandon McManus, per me and @MikeGarafolo, the latest in Los Angeles’ kicker saga. He worked out today, along with FA K Matt Prater,” NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported on X on October 20. “McManus most recently kicked for the #Packers and #Broncos.” The #Rams are signing veteran kicker Brandon McManus, per me and @MikeGarafolo, the latest in Los Angeles’ kicker saga. He worked out today, along with FA K Matt Prater. McManus most recently kicked for the #Packers and #Broncos . pic.twitter.com/eyzO9QmQjt — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 20, 2026 The news naturally drew attention locally, with McManus last kicking for the Broncos just four seasons ago. That was one year before Wil Lutz followed head coach Sean Payton in being traded to Denver from the New Orleans Saints . McManus entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent. He first signed with the Indianapolis Colts, also spending time with the Green Bay Packers , New York Giants, Jacksonville Jaguars, and Washington Commanders. Ex-Broncos K Brandon McManus Signs With Rams McManus beat out Prater, whom he replaced as the Broncos kicker in 2014, for the job with the Rams . He replaces Blake Grupe, another former UDFA who also notably made history as a member of the Colts, who suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 6. That is just one connection. The Rams signed Grupe to their 53-man roster off the New York Jets’ practice squad to replace Harrison Mevis following a rocky start to the season. Mevis notably spent time with the Jets (and Carolina Panthers ) before joining the Rams in 2025. He (also notably) had his best game of the 2026 regular season in Week 3 against the Broncos, going 4-for-4 on field goals. He also connected on both of his extra point attempts. McManus had an 81.4% conversion rate on field goals during his Broncos tenure and an 82% career mark. Even more than the Broncos, the Rams’ season has gotten off to a rocky start after high hopes coming into the campaign. It remains to be see if McManus can help turn things around for the Rams, but the ex-Broncos kicker is the latest to try. item.title: Tanner LaTorre captures medalist honors, leads Ichabod Crane to Section 2 boys' golf crown
item.description: Tanner Latorre of Ichabod Crane hits a fairway shot on the 6th hole during the high school boys' golf, Class C/D championship at Fairways of Halfmoon on Tuesday, Oct. 20, 2026, in Mechanicville, N.Y. (Lori Van Buren/Times Union) (Lori Van Buren/Times Union) MECHANICVILLE - Only three scores from each school counted toward determining a team winner Tuesday in the Section 2 Class C-D golf championship at the Fairways of Halfmoon. When one of the players shoots even par, a school's chances of winning rise significantly. Tanner LaTorre, a two-time Section 2 individual champion from Ichabod Crane, matched par 72 to earn medalist honors and led the Riders to a seven-stroke victory in the team competition. LaTorre, a senior who was runner-up at last week's sectional tournament after winning the previous two years, was six strokes clear of Greenwich's Brett Traver and Coxsackie's Nico Galante in the individual standings. LaTorre carded three birdies and three bogeys. The Riders got an 88 from LaTorre's brother Mason and a 94 from Keegan Mullins to post a seven-shot victory over Voorheesville, whose three players were within four shots of each other. Each of the 24 teams brought four players. The bottom score wasn't included in the team total. "It definitely helps," first-year coach Cameron Holzhauer said of having the elder LaTorre. "He's a good guy to watch. He's very special. They all have learned so much from him. He's been great to the young guys on the team, too. It's been great having him all year long. He's a big leader." Tanner LaTorre couldn't stay around for the awards presentation - or interviews - because he was getting his senior photo taken, so Mason met with the media. The LaTorres first got media reps in 2022 when both qualified for the Drive, Chip and Putt national finals in Augusta, Ga. "I don't really know (what to expect), because I didn't really know the other teams that well," Mason said. "I don't know if we were good enough, especially because we lost a lot of people. We lost two seniors last year that were pretty good." Saratoga Catholic finished third, nine behind the Riders. Defending C-D champion La Salle has moved up to Class B. Ichabod Crane finished second last year competing in Class B. "I'm lucky to have so many great golfers with me," Holzhauer said. "It's been a great year. It was awesome to watch them today. They played great all the way through. "We graduated a lot of guys last year. At the beginning we were piecing together the top six, but they all made huge leaps to get to where they were. It was awesome to see some of the guys that really weren't golfers before the season take huge leaps." Classes A and B will conduct separate tournaments, playing simultaneously, on Wednesday. item.title: Liverpool Player Ratings v Villarreal: Ngumoha Gets A Nine in Comeback Win
item.description: Liverpool made it nine points out of nine in the Champions League as they came from behind for the second game in a row to beat Villarreal at Anfield Goals from Alexis Mac Allister in both halves, Florian Wirtz and Ronald Araujo with one each, and helped massively by an elite individual performance from Rio Ngumoha secured a 4-2 win on the night. Here are our player ratings (out of 10) following this dramatic victory under the Merseyside lights. Alisson Becker - 7/10 Despite conceding three goals, he could do very little about any of them, with all three coming from lapses in concentration from one of the players in front of him. Kostas Tsimikas - 6/10 Didn't do anything wrong, but also offered very little going forward. He was found too often being physically dominated, and taking too long to make decisions when releasing the ball. Virgil van Dijk - 7/10 A rollercoaster of a performance for the Liverpool skipper. The bad came in the first five minutes, when he misplaced a header, allowing an onrushing Villarreal attacker to steal the ball and put the Reds 1-0 down. IMAGO/Pro Shots But from that moment onwards, the Dutch defender only grew into the game, like LFC overall, and he made several key blocks, tackles and interceptions. Jeremy Jacquet - 7.5/10 A flawless performance again from Jeremy Jacquet , and he is a player who is growing game by game, adapting to new pressures and surroundings perfectly. Ronald Araujo - 7/10 The Uruguayan only played the first 45 minutes, which concerned fans, but Iraola confirmed after the game that his withdrawal was not injury-related . As for his performance, it was a mixed bag. He was massively out of position for the second goal and was found losing the ball too often in the middle of the pitch, leaving huge spaces behind. But this is clearly tactical from Iraola, and Araujo made up for his error with a crucial equaliser right before the break. Trey Nyoni - 7/10 The 19-year-old was everywhere during this game, whether it was covering as a centre back when others went forward, or making line-breaking sprints forward himself; he was a solid contributor to this victory. Alexis Mac Allister - 8/10 He started the game off the pace, like a lot of the Liverpool players, but scored two crucial goals that helped turn a 2-0 deficit into a 4-3 win. Cody Gakpo - 6.5/10 A quiet game from Gakpo, massively outshone by his young counterpart on the opposite flank, but he has just returned from injury, and it was good to see him get a full 90 minutes. IMAGO/BSR Agency Ryan Gravenberch - 7/10 Struggled in the more advanced role he would play for most of the game. Playing at right-back for the second half, he was top-tier and nullified any threat posed down his side. Rio Ngumoha - 9/10 Fantastic, marvellous, and incredible are just a few of the words that could be used to describe Rio Ngumoha's performance in this game. Even when his side was struggling to settle into the game, he was the one trying to make something happen. IM

item.title: Panthers 1st-Round Rookie Breaks Silence on Possible Benching
item.description: Monroe Freeling Getty Carolina Panthers OT Taylor Moton Getty The Carolina Panthers are going to have a tough decision to make at tackle moving forward. First-round rookie Monroe Freeling might end up seeing the bench despite being healthy, while Taylor Moton and Rasheed Walker start. However, the 19th overall pick is viewing the step back as a learning experience. He opened up on what he has learned from Moton already. #Panthers tackle Monroe Freeling is focused on getting better at his craft and getting healthy. But he’s learned a lot from Taylor Moton. A fun story about a rookie learning from a vet here: pic.twitter.com/gsMESjZKZH — Alex Zietlow (@alexzietlow05) October 19, 2026 “I sit right next to him in meetings and see the amount of notes he takes,” said Freeling about what he learned from Moton. “Even if he heard it a 1,000 times and he’s been playing for ten years.” Freeling noted it is more than just film study and note-taking. He saw how Moton would work on technique at any time of the day. “Even when he wasn’t even playing, I’d be sitting next to him in the meeting room, and he’d actually be doing (pass blocking) sets, like in his chair,” added Freeling. Freeling noted that while he wants to start, his goal right now is to watch Moton and get healthy. Carolina Panthers Rookie Monroe Freeling Opens Up on Injury and Possible Benching Getty Carolina Panthers OT Taylor Moton Freeling has a good attitude about where he stands and what his focus is. “I can sit and be like, I don’t know what I’m doing, or I can sit and be like, well, I know what I can do and that’s get healthy,” said Freeling on his mentality with the possibility of being benched. After Moton returned in Week 7 and Rasheed Walker played well at left tackle, head coach Dave Canales noted that it will be a challenge for the Panthers rookie to get back into the lineup. “So that’s a good challenge for Monroe to see how he responds to the training, the treatment, and to see if he shows us how ready he is to play,” said Canales on Monday. “And then how do we play him? So all those questions we have to figure out.” Freeling noted that he enjoyed watching Moton play for the first time and that he learned a lot. “It was awesome to see T-Mo because you never really know,” said Freeling. “I don’t really know what to expect. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . A few days ago, Phoenix Suns governor Mat Ishbia and former Suns star Kevin Durant had a bit of a spat on social media. Ishbia’s quote regarding “throwing money at the problem” not being the solution made the rounds on social media, and he namedropped Durant, saying that bringing in someone like the two-time NBA Finals MVP doesn’t guarantee team success. Durant did not take too kindly to seeing his name get dragged around. The Suns governor then replied by saying that Durant, who is now with the Houston Rockets, may have simply seen the quote out of context. Moreover, he clarified that he didn’t necessarily blame Durant for the Suns’ disappointing finishes in his two-and-a-half seasons with the team. Ishbia’s stance regarding the matter hasn’t changed, and he doubled down on his defense after coming under fire for his remarks. He just kind of read some headline rather than actually watching the video, and sometimes he does that. And so he misunderstood it, and I figured I’d clarify it for him. But I feel good about what I said about the NBA and how it works,” Ishbia said in an interview posted by women’s basketball insider Khristina Williams. Phoenix Mercury and Suns owner Mat Ishbia says he doesn’t regret recent social media frenzy with Kevin Durant . pic.twitter.com/BfmM5zMLKV — Khristina (@Khristina) October 20, 2026 Ishbia purchased the Suns franchise for $4 billion in December 2022 after a scandal brought an end to Robert Sarver’s ownership of the team. He would then urge the front office to be aggressive; they broke up the core that made it to the 2021 NBA Finals by trading Mikal Bridges, Cam Johnson, and Jae Crowder, along with significant draft assets, to bring in Durant . They would then make more changes to the roster after losing in the second round of the playoffs in 2023, trading away Deandre Ayton to acquire Jusuf Nurkic and Grayson Allen. Moreover, they sent floor general Chris Paul away in a trade for Bradley Beal. They would then get swept in the first round of the 2024 NBA playoffs and they would miss the postseason entirely in 2025. The Suns traded Durant to the Rockets last year for a package headlined by Dillon Brooks and Jalen Green, surprisingly making it to the playoffs. And for supporters hoping to preserve one of the sport’s oldest racing facilities, the latest decision raises the stakes considerably. Nashville Fairgrounds Racing Ban Petition Clears Major Hurdle The Davidson County Election Commission voted 4-0, with one commissioner abstaining, to certify a petition seeking a change to Nashville’s Metro Charter that would ultimately end auto racing at the Fairgrounds. The vote came despite election officials rejecting 27,567 of the 75,246 signatures reviewed during the verification process. According to figures reported by Daily Downforce , officials accepted 47,679 signatures, exceeding the required 40,194 by 7,485. That means more than one-third of the signatures reviewed didn’t count, but organizers still gathered enough valid signatures to advance their effort. Its stated objective is to bring racing at the venue to an end. Speedway Supporters Challenge Petition as Legal Fight Continues Certification doesn’t mean Nashville Fairgrounds Speedway is closing, nor does it guarantee the proposal will appear before voters without further challenges. Speedway supporters have raised questions about how signatures were collected, including allegations that some residents’ names appeared on petition sheets without their permission. Other residents have alleged that canvassers misrepresented the petition’s purpose, including claims that they were told the speedway was already headed for demolition or that the proposal primarily concerned affordable housing. Restore Our Fairgrounds disputes those allegations. Coalition representatives have said canvassers were instructed to accurately explain the petition and that verified signature withdrawal requests were honored. Those competing claims have not been resolved by the commission’s certification vote. A court hearing scheduled for Oct. 27 could help determine how disputed signature withdrawals are handled and whether the petition can continue toward a public vote. For now, the certified signature count is enough to keep the effort alive. What Does This Mean for NASCAR’s Return to Nashville Fairgrounds? The timing presents another complication for Speedway Motorsports, which has spent years pursuing a renovation agreement that could make the historic short track suitable for NASCAR’s national series. The Cup Series hasn’t raced at Nashville Fairgrounds Speedway since 1984. Although the venue continues to host local and regional competition, a modernized facility has long been viewed as a possible route back to NASCAR’s premier level. Dale Earnhardt Jr. has also been among the prominent voices advocating for the track’s preservation and revival. But the proposed charter amendment could threaten far more than a potential Cup Series return. If approved and implemented, it would put the continuation of auto racing at the Fairgrounds itself in jeopardy. The proposal also doesn’t establish a funded housing development that would automatically replace the racetrack. It addresses the future use of the property, not a finalized construction project. Nashville voters could ultimately weigh in during a proposed August 2027 referendum, provided the petition survives its remaining legal challenges. The next immediate date to watch is Oct. 27, when the dispute over signature withdrawals is scheduled to return to court. Until then, Nashville Fairgrounds Speedway remains operational. But the campaign to end racing there has now cleared a substantial procedural obstacle, despite tens of thousands of signatures being rejected. As for Philadelphia, the team is dealing with several injuries, according to the latest available injury report. Former Knicks player Ariel Hukporti is out with a season-ending Achilles tear. Big men Tacko Fall and Dominic Barlow are also out, while Dean Wade , Adem Bona, and Anfernee Simons are listed as questionable. item.title: Why Isn’t Tacko Fall Playing Tonight? How Tall 76ers Center is Missing vs. Knicks
item.description: CAMDEN, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 28: Tacko Fall #99 of the Philadelphia 76ers poses for a portrait during media day at the Philadelphia 76ers Training Complex on September 28, 2026 in Camden, New Jersey. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) Getty The Philadelphia 76ers brought aboard the gigantic Tacko Fall for the 2026-27 NBA season. He’s impossible to miss. Every time the LeBron James-led Sixers play on a national broadcast, Fall will be there on the screen somewhere, looking super tall. The 76ers, though, won’t be able to rely on Fall in a bench big role to begin the campaign, though. Fall is out for their season opener on Tuesday night against the New York Knicks. Why Isn’t Tacko Fall Playing Tonight? Fall isn’t playing on the opening night of the 2026-27 NBA season for the 76ers against the Knicks due to injury. The center was injured on the second day of training camp when he strained his left hip. That’s the injury that had him ruled out for Tuesday night. 76ers head coach Nick Nurse had initially called it a “hip thing,” and an MRI revealed the official left hip strain diagnosis. On Oct. 1, the 76ers announced that Fall would miss at least two weeks. The timeline has clearly extended beyond that, as opening night is about three weeks since that announcement. Fall didn’t get into a game in the preseason for the 76ers. Philadelphia likely wasn’t planning on having Fall for too many minutes, so it’s probably not a huge loss, but it does remove the entertainment factor of having such a big player on the floor for Philadelphia. How Tall is Tacko Fall? Fall is officially listed at 7-foot-6. There have been only a few players in basketball history who have measured that tall or taller. Tallest Players in NBA History The two tallest players in NBA history were listed at 7-foot-7: Manute Bol and Gheorghe Muresan. Fall is 7-foot-6. That’s the same height as Shawn Bradley and Yao Ming. The Spurs have listed Victor Wembanyama at different heights during his NBA career, and he was listed at 7-foot-4 in the 2025-26 season. The Grizzlies ‘ Zach Edey is also 7-foot-4. For the sake of a 76ers comparison, Joel Embiid is listed at 7-feet tall. He’ll even look a bit short when he stands next to Fall this season. item.title: Ryan Day teases potential Julian Sayin replacement as Ohio State QB amid injury update
item.description: Ryan Day teases potential Julian Sayin replacement as Ohio State QB amid injury update originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Ohio State coach Ryan Day didn't mince words when addressing the health of Julian Sayin, a junior quarterback who had already been off to a fast start this season before suffering an elbow injury during last Saturday's 19-15 win against the Indiana Hoosiers in Bloomington. With Sayin likely done for the season, attention now turns to who is up next at arguably football's most important position. Day said Tuesday he hasn't decided which quarterback from the depth chart will replace Sayin, but he praised Luke Fahey despite not registering a completion last week. "He's an extremely hard worker," Day said of Fahey. "He puts a lot of hours in. He's extremely competitive. "He has a moxie about him. He has a competitiveness about him. We’re always looking for quarterbacks who are obsessed with being great. And, I think when you get around Luke, you can see how important it is to him. He puts a lot of work in." MORE: College Football Playoff bracket for Week 8: Projecting top four seeds, first-round matchups, bubble teams Day cited how Fahey's attributes are what most of the media and the fans don't see that sets him apart from other quarterbacks he has coached. "You know, you see him [Fahey] in the off-season; he's in here early with the receivers and he's going through the [play] scripts," Day said. "He's in the meeting rooms putting in a lot of work, learning the plays." Day said, however, that Fahey's demeanor changes when shifting to live action. "When he steps in the huddle, he has got it," Day added. "The [offensive] lineman feel that. Obviously, he was a little overwhelmed...drinking through a firehose a little bit during that [Indiana] game. That's a tough spot to be in as a true freshman going into the fourth quarter like that. But even just him being out there, you can see him escape the pocket and make that play." Day said growing pains are part of growing as a young college quarterback, reiterating that he wants Fahey to use him and the coaching staff as a resource as the season and his Buckeye career move forward. MORE: College football picks, predictions against the spread for Week 8 matchups "He has got to find the speed of the game," Day said. "Settle in, which we can help him do. And then, he just has a competitiveness about him that I think is pretty contagious." In a little over a week, we'll find out if Day and the Buckeyes can trust Fahey enough to keep their potential CFP and Big Ten title hopes afloat. (Photo by Martin KEEP / AFP via Getty Images) / - IMAGE RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE - STRICTLY NO COMMERCIAL USE - Getty The Los Angeles Rams have received more concerning injury news as they attempt to turn around their disappointing start to the 2026 season. Second-year tight end Terrance Ferguson is reportedly facing an extended absence, despite approaching his first opportunity to return from injured reserve. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported Tuesday, October 20, that Ferguson is not expected to be ready when he becomes eligible to return next week. “Rams TE Terrance Ferguson, who is eligible to come off IR next week, is not expected to be ready at that time,” Schefter wrote on X. Schefter added that Ferguson’s recovery, according to one source, “will take some time.” Rams TE Terrance Ferguson, who is eligible to come off IR next week, is not expected to be ready at that time. His recovery, in the words of a source, “will take some time.” pic.twitter.com/6XukSCtU5M — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 20, 2026 The news leaves Los Angeles without a promising young offensive weapon for an undetermined period, adding another complication for head coach Sean McVay. Ferguson has missed three games since suffering an ankle injury against the Denver Broncos in Week 3. His placement on injured reserve October 2 required him to miss at least four games. The 23-year-old will complete that minimum absence when the Rams visit the Las Vegas Raiders on October 25. However, Schefter’s report indicates Ferguson is unlikely to return for the team’s Week 8 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers on November 1. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) Ferguson appeared poised for a larger role in McVay’s offense before suffering his injury. The former Oregon standout was selected in the second round of the 2025 NFL draft and flashed big-play potential during his rookie campaign, finishing with 11 receptions for 231 yards and three touchdowns. Through three appearances this season, Ferguson has recorded seven catches for 63 yards and one touchdown. His most productive performance came against the New York Giants in Week 2, when he caught six passes for 54 yards and a touchdown during a 28-6 victory. The momentum didn’t last long, however, with Ferguson sustaining a medial ankle sprain against Denver the following week. The Rams placed Ferguson on injured reserve ahead of their Week 4 contest against the Philadelphia Eagles . His absence has complicated matters for an offense that has frequently relied on multiple-tight-end formations. With no firm return date established, Los Angeles must continue planning around Ferguson’s absence rather than counting on an immediate reinforcement. (Photo by Martin KEEP / AFP via Getty Images) Ferguson’s extended absence comes at a particularly difficult time for the Rams, who have fallen to 2-4 following their 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals on October 18. Los Angeles also faces a significant injury to star receiver Davante Adams , who will likely miss six to 10 weeks after suffering a ruptured hamstring against Arizona. That leaves quarterback Matthew Stafford without two potential receiving targets as the Rams attempt to revive their struggling offense. Veteran tight ends Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson remain important pieces of the offense, while Davis Allen and rookie Max Klare provide additional depth. Parkinson delivered a crucial touchdown late against Arizona, briefly giving Los Angeles the lead before the Cardinals responded with a game-winning field goal. McVay had previously acknowledged that Ferguson’s injury would create more opportunities for Klare. “It certainly does,” McVay said earlier this month when asked whether Ferguson’s absence would increase Klare’s role. “This week will represent an opportunity for him to be able to get some reps and maybe get some good game-time action for us.” The Rams will need production from that group while Ferguson continues his recovery. item.title: Wisconsin's Braeden Carrington stays eligible after injunction | Reports
item.description: MADISON – Wisconsin men’s basketball and Braeden Carrington appear to have picked up a key victory in Carrington’s legal fight for a fifth season of eligibility. A California judge issued an injunction in the Glancey vs. NCAA case on Oct. 20 that allows Carrington and the other plaintiffs to remain eligible for a fifth season of college basketball in 2026-27, according to reports from CBS Sports' Jon Rothstein and others . The NCAA has consistently appealed rulings like this one, so Carrington’s legal fight is not necessarily over. But the injunction would keep the Wisconsin guard eligible to play in the meantime with fewer than two weeks before the regular season begins. Carrington initially became eligible when the judge granted a temporary restraining order in August , which made it hardly a surprise that the court would rule favorably on the injunction as well. The NCAA has previously expressed confidence in its legal outcomes, however, when such cases reach a higher court. “We intend to defend our rule because every time we’ve been able to defend it in front of a higher court, they’ve sided with us,” said Tim Buckley, the NCAA’s senior vice president for external affairs, in a September interview with the Journal Sentinel . Carrington has practiced with the Badgers and played in their first two exhibition games of the 2026-27 season. That included a 20-point performance on 5-of-7 shooting in the Badgers’ Oct. 15 exhibition win over UW-Green Bay. His continued eligibility is a huge plus for the Badgers after he averaged 8.3 points per game off the bench and shot 40.2% from 3-point range in his lone season in Madison. He transferred to UW after two years at Minnesota and one year at Tulsa. UW coach Greg Gard previously told reporters on Sept. 16 that the Badgers “wanted to walk down this road as far as we could until we either got a green light or a red light.” “We knew with Braeden all along it’s going to be a roller coaster, regardless of what happens on the 20th,” Gard said at UW’s local media day on Oct. 6 . “We’re prepared for that. … Since the portal and everything that has gone on in college athletics, it’s allowed us to take a little different view of everything and understand we just focus on things you can control.” This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: Wisconsin's Braeden Carrington stays eligible after injunction | Reports

item.description: Phil Foden shouted the loudest on a quiet night at the Etihad Stadium, announcing his personal return to form with an instinctive hat-trick as Manchester City dispatched AEK Athens with little fuss. Enzo Maresca had called for City to make their own noise amid the cacophony around the club but a businesslike victory in front of 20,000 fewer than watched the weekend’s win over Ipswich was required to get their Champions League back on track after suffering at the hands of Paris Saint-Germain . Those in attendance, officially 40,042 but that felt optimistic, saw Foden shine on the right wing and as a central striker, showing there is life without Erling Haaland, who watched from the bench. Admittedly, the opposition were not a match for the Premier League side, whose other goals came from Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki. Stavros Pilios’s consolation was more a reward for the boisterous fans in yellow and black, who created the atmosphere, than for the overall efforts of the visitors. Continue reading...

Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.description: A famous name and record attendances have given FCK a platform but a difficult start in Denmark’s top-flight shows success on the pitch is not guaranteed On an August day in 2024, 5,165 fans gathered at Vanløse Idrætspark to watch FC Copenhagen (FCK) take on B73 Slagelse in their first league match. item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Mikel Arteta’s new contract reflects where the power now lies at Arsenal | Ed Aarons
item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
